newsitem.title: INDIA: Aluminium prices seen firm on rising Asian demand.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium prices seen firm on rising Asian demand.

text.p: India's largest private aluminium maker said on Wednesday it saw international aluminium prices staying firm in the near term, with growing Asian demand providing Indian manufacturers with major opportunities.

"In the current fiscal, LME prices of aluminium indicate an upward trend. The outlook for the sector is very encouraging, both in the domestic and international markets," said Kumar Mangalam Birla, chairman of Hindalco Industries Ltd.
"Following the flat 1995 and 1996, international aluminium demand has gained momentum in 1997," Birla told shareholders at the company's annual general meeting.
"Most analysts predict that the sustained demand of the order of three percent will progressively exceed planned capacity addition. Strong fundamentals are expected to result in firm prices."
The Asian region is slated to be major contributor to the expected growth in international demand, Birla added. "This will provide great opportunities to all producers in India."
Domestically, Birla said, demand for aluminium continued to grow, reflecting the fourth consecutive year of growth.

"The rising importance of aluminium, increasing income levels, globalisation of the Indian market place and the efforts of industry to provide diversified and high quality products give an added impetus to this sector's growth," he said.

As part of its strategy to capitalise on these favourable factors, Birla said Hindalco intended to raise funds overseas, and seek international credit ratings before the end of the third quarter of 1997/98.
Hindalco intends shortly to commission two turbines of 70 MW each at its power plant at Renusagar the in northern Uttar Pradesh state, Birla added.
"This will take the total capacity at Renusagar power plant to 575 MW," he said. "It will also yield some surplus power that can be supplied to the grid."
Hindalco plans to augment its smelter capacity to 242,000 million tonnes per annum by the end of the financial year, Birla said.
"Work on increasing of smelter capacity to 242,000 million tonnes per annum continues," he added. "The additional capacity is expected to be commissioned in the last quarter of the current year."
As Hindalco nears the end of a 17.5-billion-rupee capital expenditure plan, Birla said it is seeking out new investment opportunities.
"In our view such opportunities should not only add value to our investors and shareholders but significnatly contribute to the national economy," he added.

The lack of a sizeable smelting capacity in southeast Asia coupled with India's potential as a manufacturing base had prompted Hindalco to study the feasibility of setting up a new venture in the eastern state of Orissa, Birla said.
"The company is examining the feasibility of a mega, integrated aluminium complex in Orissa," he said.
A nearby market and easy access to a port were factors that determined the choice of Orissa, Birla added.

"A memorandum of understanding has been signed with the Oriss Mining Corp, and the government of Orissa for two bauxite deposits given that orissa offers the best bauxite and has ample coal reserves."
But Hindalco would finally decide on the project only near the end of the fiscal year, after an ongoing techno-economic feasibility study was completed, Birla stressed.
